THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND

Statement 
(a) Doordarshan is presently providing coverage to 53.4% of area and 74.8% 
of population in the 12 hilly districts of Utaranchal region in Uttar-Pradesh with 
a network of 44 transmitters of varying powers. However, certain areas of these 
districts are not able to receive Doordarshan signals properly, primarily, due to 
obstructions and shadows arising from hilly terrains. 
(b) Tehri and Uttarkashi districts have a network of 4 and 3 transmitters 
respectively. Presently there is no proposal to set up TV transmitters at 
Chandravadni and Chamarara Devi. 
(c) Details of the transmitters installed so far in the 12 hill districts of Uttar 
Pradesh are given in the enclosed Table.

be pleased to state:

(a) whether steps have been taken by Government to modernise the 
Doordarshan Centres in the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the steps taken in this regard in Orissa during Eighth and Ninth Plan 
period; 
(d) the various modernisation programmes pending in Orissa and other States; and 
(e) the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND 
BROADCASTING AND MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW, 
JUSTICE AND COMPANY AFFAIRS (SHRI ARUN JAITLEY): (a) to (e) A 
statement is laid on the table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) and (b) It has been the constant endeavour of Doordarshan to modernise 
and upgrade its various facilities. Some of the specific projects commissioned/ 
completed by Doordarshan to modernise its facilities during 9th Plan are as follows:  
(i) New modern studios at Mumnai, Nagpur and Rajkot.  
(ii) Degital satellite uplink facilities for uplinking of its various channels such 
as DD-I, DD-II, DD-News, DD-Sports and DD-International.  
(iii) Simulcast uplinking facilities both in digital and analog at DDK Calcutta, 
Hyderabad, Trivandrum, Bangalore, Guwahati, Chennai and Mumbai.  
(iv) New automation facility at DDK, Delhi. 
In addition, state of the art equipment have Been provided to a number 
of Kendras and some old transmitters have also been replaced by new 
transmitters of higher power. 
(c) to (e) In the state of Orissa, Studio at Bhubaneswar equipped with 
modern 'equipment was commissioned during 8th Plan period and, thereafter, 
facilities at the station have been augmented from time to time. Additional studio 
equipment is envisaged to be provided Bhubaneswar studio, as part of 9th 
Plan,Besides, LPT at Baleshwar have been upgraded to 10 KW HPT, 10 KW 
HPT with 150 M tower is under installation at Sambalpur (inreplacement of 1 
KW transmitter) and a 1 KW transmitter at Berhampur (in replacement of 
present LPT). Also, the present LPTs Bargarh, Rajgangapur and Joda in Orissa 
are envisaged to be replaced by 500W Transmitters. 
Upgradation/replacement of 111 transmitters and 2 studios, besides various 
schemes relating to the provision of a dditional studio equipment, are under 
implementation in various parts of the country, including Orissa. State-wise 
details are given in the enclosed Table.

Import of used Cars 
802. SHRI VEDPRAKASH P. GOYAL: Will the Minister of COMMERCE 
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
(a) the present status of the proposal to permit import of used cars in India;
  
(b) whether any study has been conducted to assess its bad impact on 
Indian automobile industry with findings thereof; 
(c) whether similar steps have been taken in other developing countries 
also; 
(d) if so, what impact it had in those countries with details thereof; 
(e) the steps taken to safeguard the domestic automobile industry from 
cheap foreign made used cars; and 
(f) the steps Government propose to take? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY (SHRI MURASOLI 
MARAN): (a) to (0 Cars are classified under Exim Code No. 87.0 of ITC (HS) 
Classifications of Export and Import Items, 1997-2002, and import of these items 
is presently restricted. In view of India's International commitments, all 
quantitative restrictions on imports maintained by India for balance of payment 
reasons are required to be removed by 1.4.2001. 
Research and Information System for the Non Alig ned and Other 
Developing Countries (RIS), an autonomous body under the Ministry of External 
Affairs, Government of India, has conducted a study on behalf of Association 
of Indian Automobile Manufacturers on the WTO Regime and 
69 

RAJYA SABHA   [31st July, 2000] 
its implications for the Indian Automobile Industry. This study has stated that the 
implementation of the commitments undertaken by India as a member of the WTO 
will have far reaching implications for the automobile industry in India. As regards 
the impact on the domestic automobile industry in other developing countries, this 
study has stated that the countries which have allowed the import of second hand 
(used) vehicles have not been successful in establishing a competitive automobile 
industry. 
However, even after removal of quantitative restrictions the imports will 
still be subject to applic able tariffs, technical standards and environment and 
safely norms. These measures singly or in combination can be appropriately used 
to create a level playing field for the domestic automobile industry. A decision 
on this issue will be taken in due course after examining all relevant aspects.

Flouting of Indecent Exposure of Women Act 
848. SHRI RAJNATH SINGH "SURYA": Will the Minister of 
INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware that the provisions of Indecent 
Exposure of Women Act are being flouted by print and visual media; 
(b) if so, the reasons for Government being unable to keep a watch 
and check it; 
(c) whether it is a fact that certain foreign-TV channels are doing it 
with impunity; and 
(d) if so, whether Government will put a ban on it? 
111 

RAJYA SABHA   [31st July, 2000] 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND 
BROADCASTING AND MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW JUSTICE 
AND-COMPANY AFFAIRS (SHRI ARUN JAI TLEY): (a) to (d) A Doordarshan 
Broadcast Code already exists and all pr ogrammes telecast on Television by 
Doordarshan are governed by it. Doordarshan strictly abides by the provisions of 
Indecent Representation of Women Act, 1986, while telecasting its programmes. 
Doordarshan also follows the Code, which ensures that no advertisement has 
indecent, vulgar, suggestive, repulsive or offensive themes or treatment. The 
programmes of foreign satellite channels are uplinked from outside the country and, 
therefore, do not fall under the ambit of Indian laws; unless decoders are required 
for their reception. To bring the foreign satellite channels within the ambit of Indian 
laws, programme codes and standards, a comprehensive legislation is proposed for 
regulating private .< broa dcasting in the country. Cable Television Networks 
(Regulation) Act, 1995 is also proposed to be amended in order to achieve uniform 
applicability of Programme and Advertisement Codes on all satellite channels. 
All films, including advertisement films intended for public exhibition in India 
and required to be certified by the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) in 
accordance with the provisions of the Cinematograph Act, 1952 and the guidelines 
thereunder. CBFC, while examining films for certification, ensures, inter-alia, that 
human sensibilities are not offended by vu lgarity, obscenity, depravity, sex and 
violence. 
In so far as the Print Media is concerned, the Government does not interfere 
inmatters relating to the Press. The Press Council of India is a statutory authority 
established for preserving the freedom of the Press and for maintaining and 
improving the standards of newspapers and news agencies in India.

913. SHRIS. RAMACHANDRAN PILLAI: Will the Minister of 
URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the percentage of urban population living in slums in Delhi, 
Mumbai, Calcutta, Chennai, Ahmedabad, Hyderabad and other 
State capitals; and 
(b) the percentage of slum population enjoying facilities of tap 
water, proper sanitation, pucca Roads, health services, schools in 
slum areas in State Capitals, Capital-wise? 
THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION (SHRI JAGMOHAN): (a) There is no periodical 
assessment of slum population in India. However, the Town and 
Country Planning Organisation conducted a study and brought out 
a report entitled 'A Compendium on Indian Slums-1996'. 
Identified/estimated slum population of 23 metropolitan cities as 
given in the said report is enclosed (Annexure I in the Statement-I), 
this includes Delhi, Mumbai, Calcutta, Chennai Ahmedabad, 
Hyderabad, and a few State Capitals (See below). 
(b) Slum improvement is a State subject. Information regarding 
provision of water supply and sanitation facilities in the cities and 
towns is assessed on whole-town basis and not area-wise or 
category-wise. However based on the information received from the 
State PHE Departments, Water Boards etc., State-wise information in 
regard to. provision of drinking water supply facilities through House 
Service Connections.-Public St and Posts etc. and sanitation 
facilities provided through Sewerage, Low Cost Sanitation, septic 
tank etc. has been collected and  compiled. Accordingly, the 
percentage of population having access to drinking water supply 
facilities in urban areas has been assessed as about 90% and 
population provided with sewerage and sanitation facilities has been 
assessed as about 49% of the estimated urban population as on 
31.3.1997. The coverage percentage indicates accessibility only. It 
docs not indicate adequacy and equitable distribution of water 
supply as per the prescribed norms of Govt, of India. The State-wise 
coverage of urban population with water supply and sanitation 
facilities is given in Statement-II.

Policy regarding Urbanisation 
922. SHRI NARENDRA MOHAN: Will the Minister of URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to 
state: 
(a) what is the policy of Government towards urbanisation with the 
constant increase in the number of slum dwellers; 
† Original notice of the Question was received in Hindi., 
181 

RAJYA SABHA [31st July, 
2000J 
(b) whether Government are thinking of developing secondary and 
tertiary towns for this purpose; and 
(c) the steps Government propose to take to tackle the problem of 
settlement of slum dwellers and whether there is any time-frame in this 
regard? 
THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION (SHRI JAGMOHAN): (a) T he Govt, is in the process of 
finalisation of a National Urban Policy which aims at promoting sustainable, 
efficient, well-managed, and regionally balanced urban development in the 
country. In the Policy, the emphasis is on rural urban continuum and an 
articulated human settlement system with a well-defined regional hierarchy 
that integrates and strengthens the urban centres and surrounding rural 
areas. The policy would also focus on strengthening local bodies, improving 
planning, management and urban governance, reducing poverty protecting 
environment, promoting healthy and af fordable housing as well as cost 
effective and efficient infrastruc ture; and services systems and thus 
improving the quality of life of urban inhabitants. 
(b)To encourage spatial dispersal of economic development and to 
increase ihc level of infrastructure and services and employment 
opportunities in medium and small towns at an accelerated pace, in order 
to promote growth in these towns so as to reduce migration to large cities 
and proliferation of slums this Ministry is already implementing such a 
scheme viz., Integrated Development of Small and Medium Towns 
(IDSMT). 
(c) The Problem of slum dwellers has been engaging attention of the 
Government since die Second Five Year Plan. At present following two 
specific schemes for the slum dwellers are going on:— 
(i)  Environment Improvement of Urban Slums (EIUS)—It is a Stale 
sector scheme. 
(ii) National Slum Development Programme (NSDP)—Under this 
programme additional Central assistance is being given to States/ 
UTs for (the development of urban slums. 
The problem of settlement of slum dwellers in urban areas is to be 
tackled within the overall framework of the Government's policies on a 
continuous basis. Therefore, no time frame has been fixed for this purpose.
